children.value: > Fact From Story The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.

> > Fact From Story Other Google technologies, like “Featured Snippets” where Google algorithmically extracts answers from webpages, were also cited as shifting traffic away from publishers’ websites.

> > > Fact From Story In the complaint, Helena World Chronicle, which owns and publishes two weekly newspapers in Arkansas, argues that Google is “starving the free press” by sharing publishers’ content on Google, losing them “billions of dollars.”
> > > Fact From Story Google links people to publishers’ websites more than 24 billion times each month – at no cost to them.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge If a company shares content from a publisher and deprives them of revenue, that is siphoning off their content, readers, and ad revenue.
> > Fact From Story The suit points to Google’s older question-and-answer technologies, like the “Knowledge Graph” launched in May 2012, as part of the problem.
> > Commonsense Knowledge Shifting traffic away from a website reduces the ad revenue that website can generate.
> Commonsense Knowledge A class action antitrust suit can be filed when a company is believed to be engaging in anticompetitive behavior that harms others.
